security_audit.summary: Review dismissed 121 of 123 static alerts as documentation, placeholder secrets, template literals, or inert examples. Two command instructions remain medium risks because they execute project or package code. Semantic review also found an unsafe HTTP example and a harness that launches a user-selected subprocess.

remediation.issue: The complete TypeScript HTTP example can listen beyond localhost without request authentication or Origin validation.
remediation.suggestion: Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default, validate Origin and Host, require authentication, and document secure remote deployment settings.

remediation.issue: The evaluation harness launches any command supplied through its command-line options.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, document the trust boundary, reject shell intermediaries, and support an allowlist for common server runtimes.

remediation.issue: Build and Inspector instructions can execute project scripts or an unpinned package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the Inspector version and tell users to review package scripts and dependencies before running npm or npx commands.

content.value_statement: MCP integrations often fail because tools, schemas, transports, and evaluations are inconsistent. This skill provides structured TypeScript and Python guidance from design through testing.
actual_capabilities: Plans MCP tools around API endpoints and user workflows.
Guides TypeScript servers built with the MCP SDK and Zod.
Guides Python servers built with FastMCP and Pydantic.
Covers stdio and streamable HTTP transport patterns.
Defines response, pagination, annotation, and error-handling practices.
Provides an XML evaluation format and a Claude-based evaluation harness.
limitations: This skill provides guidance and examples; it does not generate a complete server without service requirements.
Example endpoints, credentials, names, and schemas are placeholders that require replacement.
The evaluation harness requires Python dependencies and an Anthropic API key.
Evaluations send questions and tool results to Anthropic, and stdio mode launches a selected local command.

use_cases.title: Integrate a service API
use_cases.description: Design and implement an MCP server with validated tools, pagination, structured responses, and clear errors.

use_cases.title: Standardize MCP delivery
use_cases.description: Create team conventions for naming, transport selection, authentication, testing, and implementation quality.

use_cases.title: Measure tool effectiveness
use_cases.description: Build read-only evaluation questions, run them against an MCP server, and review accuracy and tool feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a server
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an MCP server for [service]. Identify the main user workflows, required API endpoints, tool names, inputs, outputs, authentication, and transport.

prompt_templates.title: Build with TypeScript
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a TypeScript MCP server for [service] using the official SDK and Zod. Include [tools], pagination, structured responses, annotations, and actionable errors.

prompt_templates.title: Build with Python
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a Python FastMCP server for [service] using Pydantic. Include [tools], shared API helpers, input constraints, pagination, annotations, and secure credential handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review and evaluate
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the MCP server in [path]. Check security, schemas, tool design, transport, errors, and context efficiency. Create ten stable read-only evaluation questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation audit and evaluation design

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server that lets support agents search customers and inspect recent tickets.
output: Recommended tools: search customers, get customer details, list tickets, and get ticket details.
Each list tool includes bounded limits, pagination metadata, and stable identifiers.
Customer data uses read-only annotations and requires scoped service credentials.

output_examples.input: Review an existing TypeScript MCP server for tool quality and transport safety.
output: Tool review identifies unclear names, missing input limits, and inconsistent response formats.
Transport review checks authentication, Origin validation, host binding, and error exposure.
The final checklist separates required fixes from optional improvements.

output_examples.input: Create an evaluation plan for a project management MCP server.
output_examples.output: The plan defines ten independent read-only questions, verified answers, stable historical data, and accuracy reporting with per-tool feedback.

best_practices: Review current official MCP and SDK documentation before implementation.
Use least-privilege credentials, strict schemas, bounded pagination, and accurate tool annotations.
Pin dependencies and test compilation, transport behavior, authentication, and failure cases in a controlled environment.
anti_patterns: Do not run project commands or package installers before reviewing their source and configuration.
Do not expose streamable HTTP endpoints without authentication, Origin checks, and deliberate host binding.
Do not copy placeholder endpoints, credentials, schemas, or tool descriptions into production.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides detailed guidance for TypeScript with the MCP SDK and Python with FastMCP.

faq.question: Does it build the server automatically?
faq.answer: It guides planning, implementation, review, and evaluation. The final server still depends on your API requirements and project environment.

faq.question: Which transports are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover local stdio and remote streamable HTTP. SSE appears only for compatibility in the evaluation harness.

faq.question: How are MCP servers evaluated?
faq.answer: The included harness loads XML questions, lets Claude call server tools, compares final answers, and produces an accuracy report.

faq.question: Does evaluation require external access?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires Anthropic API access and may connect to a remote MCP endpoint or launch a local server.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use scoped environment variables or secure runtime input. Never commit real keys, print secret values, or place them in evaluation files.
